solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On the radio: state bombs archipelago

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words before it are judged by their sound

parts.note: to state is to say, and bombs are shells; the pair spoken runs 'say shells'

explanation.surface: A news broadcast reports a country dropping bombs on a group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun (a nation) but is the verb SAY; 'bombs' is the noun SHELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seychelles are a group of islands in the Indian Ocean, so the name is an example of an island chain.

clue.text: Renouncing identity Coleridge confused painter

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the poet's remaining letters are reordered
renouncing means giving something up, so these letters are dropped from the poet

parts.note: ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: The poet Coleridge, losing his sense of self, mistakes himself for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ID from COLERIDGE leaves COLERGE, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Greek-born Renaissance artist who worked in Spain.

clue.text: Completely innocent

definitions.meaning: ... as an adverb means completely, as in '... forgot'

explanation.surface: Someone declared wholly blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means entirely (clean through) and also guiltless (a clean record).

clue.text: Stress English politician has income support at first

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of the two words that come before it

explanation.surface: An English MP claims benefits, initially at least, under some strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support is a British state benefit, so the surface pictures a politician on welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is stress or prominence given to a word or idea.

clue.text: Member with desire: see her excited about cold dairy product

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
an urge is a desire

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the cold letter
excited letters are agitated, so these are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man in a state of desire tells a woman to look at something chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' signals the shuffle, giving RHEESE, and 'about' wraps that round C. 'Member' looks like a club member but is an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a strong-smelling soft cheese from Limburg, so it is a milk-based food.

clue.text: Good man with garment for flasher at disco

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: A virtuous man in a coat turns out to be an exhibitionist at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flasher' suggests an indecent exposer, but here it is a light that flashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a rapidly flashing light used at nightclubs.

clue.text: Fails to ignore 50 dandy dressers

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the word for failures

parts.note: flops are failures; as a verb, fails = flops
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Vain, overdressed men supposedly fail to notice something.
explanation.definitionFit: Fops are vain men excessively concerned with clothes, so they are showy dressers.

clue.text: Connoisseur seen around home is money wizard

indicators.note: the expert word is seen around the at-home word, enclosing it

parts.note: a fancier is an expert enthusiast
in means at home

explanation.surface: An expert seen about the house turns out to be a financial genius.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier manages large sums of money, so is a moneyed expert.

clue.text: Ghost from Hampton wandering about

indicators.note: letters wandering about stray from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spirit roams Hampton Court.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court Palace near London is famously said to be haunted.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a spectre or apparition, a synonym of ghost.

clue.text: Giant blunder on pitch disheartened Rice

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal, a blunder on the pitch

indicators.note: losing the heart means only the outer letters of the name are kept

explanation.surface: A huge mistake on the field leaves a player called Rice dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' reads as an adjective for the blunder, but it is the definition. Rice loses its middle IC to give RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous man-eating giant of folk tales.

clue.text: European Arab protecting monarch in Knock

indicators.note: one group of letters sits in the word for criticise harshly

parts.note: to knock is to criticise, to pan

indicators.note: the Arab word wraps around the royal letters like a guard

parts.note: an Omani is an Arab from Oman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A man from the Middle East shields a king during a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like a blow in the scuffle but means criticise; 'European' looks like a nationality contrasted with Arab, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pomeranian is someone from Pomerania, a region on the Baltic coast of Poland and Germany.

clue.text: An heir put out causing damage to corporation?

indicators.note: letters that are put out are disturbed, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: An upset heir harms the company he is due to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is the business sense in the surface but means a pot belly here, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is a rupture of the abdominal wall, an injury to the belly, which is jokingly called a corporation.

clue.text: In Beirut perhaps an inhabitant there?

definitions.text: In Beirut perhaps an inhabitant there?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A question about who might live in the Lebanese capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a resident of a city such as Beirut is a city dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbanite is a city dweller, and Beirut is a large city, so its residents qualify.

clue.text: Disgust where Heather defends expletive

indicators.note: the plant word surrounds and shields the swear word

parts.note: ling is a name for common heather
an oath is a swear word

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather sticks up for someone's swearing, to general revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike or revulsion, a synonym of disgust as a noun.

clue.text: Drink with meal can give one wind, expert admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the skilled word goes inside the winding word

parts.note: to wind is to twine, to coil round
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: Drinking with dinner can bring on flatulence, an expert concedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' suggests flatulence but is the verb to coil, TWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Table wine is ordinary wine served with food at the dinner table.

clue.text: Female having Irish mother

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A woman whose mother is from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma is a woman's given name, an example of a female.

clue.text: Modern philosopher gathering momentum

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the wise word holds the speed word

parts.note: a sage is a wise thinker
pace means speed or momentum

explanation.surface: A contemporary thinker builds up speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age means very up-to-date, ultra-new in style.

clue.text: Small taxi: one shouldn't pick it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A little cab you would be wise not to choose for a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick' suggests choosing a taxi, but it means picking at a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the crust over a healing wound, which people are told not to pick at.

clue.text: League accountant shows impatience when driving

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
an impatient driver hoots the horn

explanation.surface: An accountant gets irritable behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: In cahoots means in league, working together secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cahoots means partnership or collusion, as in being in league with someone.

clue.text: Scotsman to invest capital short after run on bank

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay comes after the cricket letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: to invest is to surround, so the Scots name surrounds the trimmed city

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the city is cut off

parts.note: Paris is the French capital

explanation.surface: A Scot plans to put money in after a rush on a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run on bank' reads as a financial panic and 'invest' as putting money in; here 'on bank' is the definition, meaning by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Riparian describes things situated on a river bank, such as plants or property.

clue.text: Second drink from anonymous person?

definitions.meaning: one more glass, a further round
... is a placeholder name for an unnamed person, as on team sheets

explanation.surface: A refill handed over by an unknown donor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A. N. Other' is a British placeholder used when a player or speaker is not yet named.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for one more drink is having a further one, and A.N. Other stands for an unnamed person.

clue.text: Detective Inspector needing European aerial

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A police inspector requires a foreigner's help.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipole is a type of radio antenna made of two rods.

clue.text: Shy right away from utter nonsense

indicators.note: something taken away from a phrase is removed, so a letter goes

parts.note: utter and sheer both mean complete
pish is an old word for nonsense

explanation.surface: A timid person backs off from total rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like a verb, to speak, but is the adjective SHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means embarrassed and bashful, close to shy.

clue.text: Ruminant eating everything green

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes inside the animal

parts.note: a cow is a ruminant, chewing the cud
all means everything

explanation.surface: A cow munches all the green grass in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the colour of what is eaten but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means inexperienced and immature, the sense of green as untried.

clue.text: Rose suddenly turned pale with temperature

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rose abruptly went white with fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as the flower but is the past tense of rise. PALE rearranged gives LEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt means jumped up, rose quickly.

clue.text: Mikado for instance sending one manager into stupor?

indicators.note: into puts the person words inside the word for unconsciousness

parts.note: a coma is a deep stupor
I is the Roman numeral for one
a coper is one who copes, a manager

explanation.surface: Someone is sent into a daze by a Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.walkthrough: A coper is one who copes, so a manager in the sense of someone who manages a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, a classic light humorous stage work with songs.

clue.text: Hard to interrupt unstoppable service — it's long

indicators.note: the hardness letter breaks into the tennis word

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve the receiver cannot return
H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencils

explanation.surface: A tough player breaks up an unreturnable serve in a lengthy match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' reads as describing the service, but as a verb it means yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for it, to yearn.

clue.text: Discussed division of the church in land surrounded

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: an aisle is a side division of a church

explanation.surface: A church section was talked over as the building stood surrounded.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land with water all around it.

clue.text: Simple copper perhaps suspicious when wife leaves

parts.note: copper is an example of a chemical element

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they are gone, so a letter is removed

parts.note: wary means suspicious

explanation.surface: A policeman becomes simple-minded and distrustful after his wife walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or easy, so it is a synonym of simple.
